info.title: anony-mail API
info.summary: REST + Server-Sent Events API for an inbound-only disposable email backend.
info.description:
anony-mail is an inbound-only disposable email (temp mail) backend. It receives mail over SMTP for throwaway addresses and exposes it through this HTTP API. It does **not** send mail.

### Conventions
- **Base path:** every resource endpoint lives under `/api`; the health check is at `/healthz`.
- **Content type:** request and response bodies are JSON, except attachment downloads (raw bytes) and the events endpoint (an SSE stream).
- **Addresses are case-insensitive.** They are lowercased server-side before lookup or creation, so `Foo@Example.com` and `foo@example.com` refer to the same mailbox.
- **Timestamps** are UTC in RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 format (e.g. `2026-07-01T11:23:45.123456Z`).
- **IDs** (message and attachment) are UUIDs (v4).

### Errors
On failure the API returns the matching HTTP status code with a JSON body of the form `{ "error": "message" }`. A `500` always reports a generic `"internal server error"` message; details are logged server-side.

### Authentication (owner tokens)
Reads are open by design (temp mail is semi-public): anyone who knows an address can fetch the mailbox, its messages, attachments, and the SSE stream. **Destructive and lifecycle operations are gated by an owner token**: creating an address returns a one-time `owner_token` (`am_` + 43 base64url chars). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <owner_token>` for extend, rotate, mailbox delete, and message delete; requests without a valid token fail with `401` and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header. The token is never returned again — store it client-side. Losing it means losing control of the mailbox (it stays readable until it expires). `POST /api/addresses/{address}/rotate` reissues the token and instantly revokes the old one.

### Tiers & client tokens (hosted instances)
Servers with `ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED=true` gate some write features per tier (see `GET /api/capabilities` → `entitlements`). Clients prove their tier by calling `POST /api/entitlements/verify` (optionally with their anonymous RevenueCat app-user id) and sending the returned signed token as `X-Client-Token` on writes. **No token simply means free tier** — it is never an error by itself. Policy rejections use the matching status code plus a machine-readable `code` field: `pro_required`, `lifetime_cap`, `mailbox_cap` (403), `client_token_expired`, `client_token_invalid`, `attestation_required` (401). Self-hosted servers default to enforcement off: every feature is available with no token.

### Client attestation (hosted instances)
Servers can additionally require proof that writes come from a genuine app build (`GET /api/capabilities` → `attestation`). iOS clients run Apple App Attest once per install (`POST /api/client/challenge` then `POST /api/client/attest`) and afterwards refresh their token with assertions (`POST /api/client/assert`); the resulting `X-Client-Token` carries the tier *and* marks the client as attested. When `attestation.required` is `true`, every mutating endpoint rejects requests without an attested token with `401` / `code: attestation_required` — reads stay open. Self-hosted servers leave this off entirely.

### Rate limiting
Requests are rate limited per client IP (general bucket plus a stricter one on address creation, and a daily per-IP address-creation quota). Exceeding a limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

### Mailbox lifecycle
Mailboxes expire after `DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 1 hour) and are periodically purged along with their messages and attachments. Use `POST /api/addresses/{address}/extend` to push the expiry back.

host.description: Hostname where your anony-mail instance is reachable.

tags.name: Capabilities
tags.description: Discover which optional server features this instance has enabled.

tags.name: Entitlements
tags.description: Free/pro tier verification (`ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED`). Purchase-based, no accounts: the app exchanges its anonymous RevenueCat app-user id for a short-lived signed client token whose tier the write endpoints enforce. Self-hosted servers leave all of this off.

tags.name: Client attestation
tags.description: Apple App Attest device verification (`APP_ATTEST_*`): challenge issuance, one-time key attestation, and assertion-based token refresh. Produces *attested* `X-Client-Token`s — the only kind accepted for writes when the server sets `CLIENT_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED=true`. Endpoints answer 503 when App Attest is not configured; self-hosted servers can ignore this feature entirely.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Discover which domains this server accepts mail for.

tags.name: Custom domains
tags.description: Bring your own domain: claim it, prove control via DNS (TXT + MX), then create mailboxes on it and receive mail. Endpoints answer 404 on servers with `CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED=false` — check `GET /api/capabilities` first. All routes except create require the domain's `amd_…` claim token, returned once by the create call.

tags.name: Mailboxes
tags.description: Create, inspect, extend, and delete disposable addresses.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: List and read received messages, and download attachments.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Live push notifications of newly arrived mail via Server-Sent Events.

tags.name: Push
tags.description: Web Push (VAPID) notifications: key discovery and per-mailbox subscription management. All push endpoints answer 503 when the server has no VAPID keypair configured.

get.description: Simple liveness probe. Always returns `200` with `{ "status": "ok" }` when the HTTP server is up. Never touches the database — use `/readyz` for readiness.

Readiness probe: verifies the storage backend answers a trivial query (`SELECT 1` on SQL backends). Returns `200` with `{ "status": "ready" }` when the service can do useful work, `503` when the database is unreachable — point load-balancer/orchestrator readiness probes here.

200.description: The service is ready to serve traffic.

example.error: store unavailable

get.description:
Reports which optional features this server instance has enabled — and the tier policy in force — so clients can adapt their UI without probing individual endpoints. Treat missing keys as `false` — new capabilities are added over time.

- `apns_push` — native iOS push (APNs credentials configured).
- `web_push` — Web Push (VAPID keypair configured).
- `custom_domains` — bring-your-own-domain endpoints are live.
- `attestation` — client-attestation posture: `supported` says the `/api/client/*` App Attest endpoints are live, `required` says every mutation demands an attested client token.
- `entitlements` — whether free/pro limits are enforced, and what each tier may do. When `enforced` is `false`, unlock everything.

200.description: The feature flags for this instance.

get.description: Returns the domains this server accepts mail for (the `DOMAINS` setting). The first entry is the default used when creating an address without specifying a domain.

post.description:
Creates a new mailbox and returns it **together with its one-time `owner_token`** — store the token client-side; it is required for extend, rotate, and all delete operations and is never returned again. The request body is **optional**:

- Omit the body entirely (or send `{}`) to get a random 10-character local part on the first configured domain.
- Provide `domain` to choose among the configured domains.
- Provide `local_part` to request a custom address. It must be 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]` and must not start or end with a separator (`.`, `_`, `-`). If the address is already taken, the request fails with `409 Conflict`.

Reserved role/validation local parts (`admin`, `postmaster`, `webmaster`, `abuse`, `ssladmin`, ... — RFC 2142 plus the CA/Browser-Forum set, extensible server-side via `RESERVED_LOCAL_PARTS`) cannot be claimed and fail with `400 Bad Request`.

Creation is rate limited per IP (including a daily quota); exceeding it fails with `429 Too Many Requests`.

On servers with custom domains enabled, `domain` may also be a **verified custom domain** — send its `amd_…` claim token as `Authorization: Bearer` (missing/wrong token fails with `401`, an unverified domain with `400`).

The new mailbox expires after the server's default TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`, 1 hour by default).

On servers with `ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED=true`, tier policy applies: custom local parts, domains beyond the free `domain_count`, and custom domains may require pro. Send the client token from `POST /api/entitlements/verify` as `X-Client-Token`; without one the request is treated as free tier.

When the token is **attested** (App Attest, `POST /api/client/attest`), the tier's `active_mailboxes` cap is enforced per device: once the device holds that many live mailboxes, creation fails with `403` / `code: mailbox_cap` until one expires or is deleted.

random.summary: Random address on the default domain (empty body)

domainOnly.summary: Random local part on a chosen domain

custom.summary: Custom local part on a chosen domain

201.description: Mailbox created. The `owner_token` appears **only** in this response (and in a rotate response); it cannot be recovered later.

401.description: The requested domain is a custom domain and the claim token is missing or wrong — or the supplied `X-Client-Token` is expired/invalid (`code` says which; refresh it via `POST /api/entitlements/verify`).

example.error: custom domains require their claim token

403.description: Rejected by tier policy (`ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED`). The `code` field says which gate: `pro_required` for custom local parts, extra domains, or custom domains on an insufficient tier; `mailbox_cap` when the attested device already holds the tier's maximum number of active mailboxes.

example.error: custom local parts require a higher tier

409.description: The requested custom address already exists.

example.error: address already exists: jane.doe@example.com

get.description: Returns the mailbox's metadata if it exists. Note that an expired-but-not-yet-purged mailbox is still returned here; compare `expires_at` against the current time to determine whether it is still active.

delete.description: Deletes the mailbox and all of its messages and attachments (cascading). Requires the owner token. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

post.description:
Pushes the mailbox's `expires_at` to now + the server default TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`). The extension is relative to the current time, not to the previous expiry. Requires the owner token (which stays the same — extending never rotates it). No request body is required.

On servers with `ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED=true`, the mailbox's total lifetime (`expires_at - created_at`, extends included) is capped per tier (`max_lifetime_seconds` in `GET /api/capabilities`). Extending past the cap returns `403` with `code: lifetime_cap`; send a pro `X-Client-Token` for the higher ceiling.

200.description: Expiry extended; the updated mailbox is returned.

403.description: Extending would exceed this tier's maximum mailbox lifetime (`code: lifetime_cap`).

example.error: extending would exceed this tier's max mailbox lifetime of 86400s

post.description: Reissues the mailbox's owner token and returns the new one; the previous token is revoked **immediately**. Use this if the token may have leaked. Requires the current owner token. No request body is required.

200.description: Token rotated. This response is the only place the new token appears.

get.description:
Returns lightweight summaries of the mailbox's messages, newest first (ordered by `received_at` then `id`, both descending). Bodies and attachment metadata are omitted here — fetch a single message for the full content. An existing mailbox with no mail returns `200` with an empty array `[]`; a missing mailbox returns `404`.

Pagination: `limit` caps the page size (default 50, max 200). `since` is a keyset cursor — pass the id of the newest message you have seen and only strictly newer messages are returned, which is the cheap way to poll for deltas (e.g. after a push notification). If the `since` message no longer exists (expired, deleted, or dropped by quota), the cursor is ignored and the newest page is returned.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of summaries to return. Values above 200 are clamped.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: return only messages strictly newer than this message id.

delete.summary: Delete all messages in a mailbox
delete.description: Deletes every message (and their attachments) in the mailbox in one call. The mailbox itself, its expiry, and its owner token are untouched. Requires the owner token.

get.description:
Returns a single message including its text and/or HTML bodies and attachment metadata. Attachment bytes are not inlined — download them individually via the attachments endpoint using each attachment's `id`.

Security note: `html_body` is untrusted, attacker-controlled markup (anyone can email the inbox). Render it only in a sandboxed iframe or after sanitization — see the schema description.

value.subject: Invoice #1042
value.text_body: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.
value.html_body: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

value.subject: Your verification code
value.text_body: Your verification code is 123456. It expires in 10 minutes.

delete.description: Deletes one message (and its attachments) from the mailbox. Requires the owner token. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

post.description: Sets the message's `seen` flag. Idempotent — marking an already-read message succeeds. Open like the read endpoints (knowing the address already grants read access), so no owner token is required.

get.description: Returns the message's original RFC 5322 bytes as received over SMTP (dot-unstuffed), served as `message/rfc822` with an attachment disposition (`{id}.eml`) and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Only available when the server runs with `STORE_RAW_MESSAGE=true`; otherwise — and for messages delivered before the toggle was enabled — this endpoint returns `404`.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment disposition named after the message id.

404.description: Message not found, or raw retention is disabled.

example.error: raw message not available (missing, or raw retention is disabled)

get.description: Streams the raw bytes of an attachment. The response's `Content-Type` is the attachment's stored MIME type, except that browser-active types (`text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`, `image/svg+xml`, `text/xml`, `application/xml`) are served as `application/octet-stream` so a crafted attachment cannot execute on the API origin — the real type remains available in the message's attachment metadata. Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `Content-Disposition` is set to `attachment` with a sanitized ASCII filename, plus an RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''…` form when the original name is non-ASCII.

Content-Type.description: The attachment's stored MIME type, e.g. `application/pdf`. Browser-active types are replaced with `application/octet-stream`.

Content-Disposition.description: Download disposition with a sanitized ASCII filename, plus an RFC 5987 `filename*` form for non-ASCII names.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Always `nosniff`: forbids MIME sniffing of the download.

404.description: The attachment (or its message/mailbox) was not found.

example.error: attachment not found

get.description: Reports which push channels this server can deliver on: `webpush` (browsers/PWAs via VAPID) and `apns` (native iOS apps). Use it to decide whether to prompt the user for notification permission at all.
Returns the server's VAPID public key. Pass it (decoded from base64url) as `applicationServerKey` to `PushManager.subscribe` in the browser.

post.summary: Register a push subscription (Web Push or APNs)
post.description:
Registers a push subscription for this mailbox so new-mail notifications reach the device. Requires the owner token. Two shapes share this endpoint:

- **Web Push** (browser/PWA): send `PushSubscription.toJSON()`, i.e. `{ endpoint, keys: { p256dh, auth } }`.
- **APNs** (native iOS app): send `{ device_token }` — the hex token from `didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken`.

The `kind` field is optional; it is inferred from which identifier is present. Subscribing to a channel the server has no credentials for answers `503` (check `GET /api/push/config` first). Idempotent per `(mailbox, endpoint/token)`: re-subscribing refreshes the record instead of creating a duplicate. The number of subscriptions per mailbox (all kinds combined) is capped server-side (`MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_MAILBOX`, default 5).

requestBody.description: A Web Push subscription or an APNs device token.

delete.description: Unregisters the subscription identified by its Web Push `endpoint` or APNs `device_token` (provide either). Requires the owner token. Works even when the server currently has no push credentials, so clients can always clean up.

404.description: The mailbox or subscription was not found.

example.error: subscription not found

post.description:
Claims a domain you own and returns the DNS records to publish plus the **one-time `claim_token`** (`amd_…`) — store it client-side; it gates every other operation on the domain (status, verify, delete, and creating mailboxes on it) and is never returned again.

Publish both records, then call the verify endpoint:

- **TXT** at `_anonymail.<domain>` with the returned `txt_record` value.
- **MX** at `<domain>` pointing to the returned `mx_target` (any priority).

The server's own domains (and their subdomains) cannot be claimed and fail with `400 Bad Request`. Claims are strictly rate limited per IP, including a daily quota (`MAX_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_PER_IP_PER_DAY`); exceeding it fails with `429 Too Many Requests`.

On servers with `ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED=true`, claiming a domain requires a tier whose policy allows custom domains (pro by default) — send the client token as `X-Client-Token`, otherwise the request is treated as free tier and rejected with `403` / `code: pro_required`.

201.description: Domain claimed, status `pending`. The `claim_token` appears **only** in this response.

401.description: The supplied `X-Client-Token` is expired or invalid (`code` says which; refresh it via `POST /api/entitlements/verify`).

example.error: client token expired, call POST /api/entitlements/verify again

403.description: This tier may not claim custom domains (`code: pro_required`).

example.error: custom domains require a higher tier
domain already claimed: mail.mycorp.com

get.description: Returns the claim's current status and the DNS records to publish. Requires the claim token.

delete.description: Deletes the claim. Inbound mail and new mailbox creation on the domain stop immediately; existing mailboxes live out their TTL. Requires the claim token.

post.description:
Looks up the TXT and MX records live and persists the outcome, returning per-record results. When both checks pass the domain becomes `verified`: the server accepts mail for it and mailboxes can be created on it.

Verified domains are re-checked daily in the background. A domain whose DNS stays broken for more than a ~48h grace window flips to `failed` (mail and creates stop); a later successful verify restores it.

Runs are throttled per domain (roughly one every 10 seconds); calling faster answers `429`. Requires the claim token. No request body.

200.description: Checks ran; the returned `status` reflects the persisted outcome.
An open `text/event-stream`. Each `message` event carries a JSON `MailEvent` in its `data` field.

schema.description:
SSE-framed stream. Each record is `event: message
data: <MailEvent JSON>

`. See the MailEvent schema for the data shape.

post.summary: Verify a purchase and mint a tier token
post.description:
Checks the pro entitlement for the given anonymous RevenueCat app-user id and returns a signed client token carrying the resulting tier (`free` or `pro`). Omit the id (or the whole body) for a free-tier token. Send the token as `X-Client-Token` on writes while it is valid, and call this endpoint again to refresh it — renewal re-checks the purchase, so lapsed subscriptions degrade to free within the token TTL.

Tokens from this endpoint are **unattested**: on servers where `GET /api/capabilities` reports `attestation.required: true` they do not satisfy the write gate — use `POST /api/client/attest` / `assert` instead, which run the same tier check and mint an attested token.

Available whenever the server has a `TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY` (503 otherwise); `ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCED` only controls whether write endpoints check the token. Shares the strict address-creation rate-limit budget.

200.description: Token minted. `tier` reflects the purchase check (`free` when no id was sent or the entitlement is inactive).

503.description: Entitlements are not configured on this server (no `TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY`), or the upstream purchase check is temporarily unavailable — keep the current token and retry later.

example.error: entitlements are not configured on this server

post.description:
Returns a single-use challenge for the attest/assert flows. Feed its SHA-256 (of the UTF-8 string) to `DCAppAttestService` as the `clientDataHash`, then send the same string back in the follow-up call. A challenge can be consumed exactly once and expires after `expires_in` seconds — request a fresh one per attempt.

Available whenever App Attest is configured (`APP_ATTEST_TEAM_ID` + `APP_ATTEST_BUNDLE_ID` + `TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY`); 503 otherwise. Shares the strict address-creation rate-limit budget. No request body.

post.summary: Attest a device key and mint an attested token
post.description:
One-time device registration. Verifies the App Attest attestation object locally (certificate chain to Apple's App Attest root CA, app id, challenge hash), stores the device's public key, and returns an **attested** client token — same shape as `POST /api/entitlements/verify`, but it also satisfies servers with `CLIENT_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED=true`. Include the anonymous RevenueCat app-user id so the token carries the right tier.

Run once per app install with the result of `DCAppAttestService.generateKey` + `attestKey`; afterwards refresh tokens with `POST /api/client/assert`. Rejections are coded (`400`): `invalid_challenge` for an unknown, expired, or reused challenge, `invalid_attestation` when verification fails.

400.description: The challenge or the attestation was rejected — `code` says which: `invalid_challenge` (request a new challenge and retry) or `invalid_attestation` (the attestation object failed verification).

example.error: challenge unknown, expired, or already used; request a new one

post.summary: Refresh an attested token with an assertion
post.description:
Refreshes the attested client token by proving possession of a previously registered device key: call `DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion` over the SHA-256 of a fresh challenge and send the result. The assertion's signature counter must strictly increase, which blocks replay — on a counter conflict just retry with a fresh challenge.

Call it whenever the current token nears `expires_at` (the tier is re-checked on every refresh). Coded rejections: `invalid_challenge` and `invalid_assertion` (`400`), plus `attestation_required` (`401`) when the key id is unknown — for example pruned after long inactivity — in which case run the attest flow again.

200.description: Assertion verified; fresh attested token minted.

400.description: The challenge or the assertion was rejected — `code` says which: `invalid_challenge` (request a new challenge and retry) or `invalid_assertion` (bad signature, wrong app id, or a non-increasing counter).

example.error: assertion counter conflict, retry with a fresh challenge

401.description: The key id is not registered on this server (never attested, or pruned after long inactivity). Run `POST /api/client/attest` again.

example.error: unknown key id, attest this device first

ownerToken.description: Per-mailbox owner token returned once by `POST /api/addresses` (and by rotate). Format: `am_` + 43 base64url characters. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <owner_token>`.

claimToken.description: Per-domain claim token returned once by `POST /api/custom-domains`. Format: `amd_` + 43 base64url characters. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <claim_token>`.

clientToken.name: X-Client-Token
clientToken.description: Signed tier token (12h TTL) from `POST /api/entitlements/verify` (unattested) or `POST /api/client/attest` / `assert` (attested, App Attest). Optional: on enforcing servers a request without it is treated as free tier — unless the server reports `attestation.required`, in which case mutations demand an attested one. `Authorization` stays reserved for owner/claim tokens, so both can be sent together.

AddressPath.name: address
AddressPath.description: Full email address of the mailbox. Case-insensitive (lowercased server-side). The `@` may be sent literally or percent-encoded as `%40`.

DomainPath.name: domain
DomainPath.description: The claimed custom domain. Case-insensitive (lowercased server-side).

BadRequest.description: The request was invalid (e.g. unknown domain or malformed `local_part`).

unknownDomain.summary: Domain is not in the server's DOMAINS list

value.error: local_part must be 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-' and not start/end with a separator

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid owner token. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

TooManyRequests.description: A per-IP rate limit or quota was exceeded. Retry later.

example.error: daily address creation limit reached

AttestationNotConfigured.description: App Attest is not configured on this server (`APP_ATTEST_TEAM_ID` / `APP_ATTEST_BUNDLE_ID` / `TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY` unset). Check `GET /api/capabilities` → `attestation.supported` before calling.

example.error: app attestation is not configured on this server

PushNotConfigured.description: The server has no credentials for the requested push channel (no VAPID keypair for `webpush`, no APNs key for `apns`). Check `GET /api/push/config`.

example.error: apns not configured

MailboxNotFound.description: No mailbox exists for this address.

example.error: mailbox not found

MessageNotFound.description: No such message in this mailbox.

example.error: message not found

DomainNotFound.description: No custom-domain claim exists for this domain.

example.error: domain not found

InternalError.description: An unexpected server error occurred. Details are logged server-side.

example.error: internal server error

CapabilitiesResponse.description: Feature flags for this server instance. Treat missing keys as `false`.

apns_push.description: Native iOS push is available (APNs credentials configured).

web_push.description: Web Push is available (VAPID keypair configured).

attestation.description: Client-attestation posture (Apple App Attest). When `required` is `true`, obtain an attested token via `POST /api/client/attest` before any write.

required.description: Mutating endpoints demand an attested client token.

entitlements.description: Tier policy in force. When `enforced` is `false` clients should unlock everything and show no paywalls (the self-host experience).

domain.description: A domain you control, e.g. `mail.mycorp.com`. Lowercased server-side; a trailing dot is tolerated. The server's own domains and their subdomains are rejected.

DnsCheck.description: The outcome of one DNS verification check.

record.description: Which record was checked: the TXT challenge at `_anonymail.<domain>` or the MX at `<domain>`.

ok.description: Whether the expected value was found.

expected.description: The value the domain owner is expected to publish.

found.description: What DNS actually returned (comma-joined when multiple records exist), or `null` when nothing resolved.

CustomDomain.description: A custom-domain claim. `claim_token` appears only in the create response; `checks` only in verify responses.

status.description: Claim lifecycle: `pending` until DNS checks pass, `verified` while they hold (mail flows), `failed` after they stay broken past the ~48h grace window.

txt_record.description: Value to publish as a TXT record at `_anonymail.<domain>`.

mx_target.description: Host the domain's MX record must point at (any priority).

claim_token.description: The one-time `amd_…` bearer token that owns this claim. Returned **only** by the create call.

verified_at.description: When DNS checks last passed (UTC). Absent while never verified.

checks.description: Per-record results of the verification run (verify responses only).

CreateAddressRequest.description: Options for creating a mailbox. Every field is optional; an empty object (or no body) yields a random address on the first configured domain. Unknown fields are ignored.

local_part.description: Custom local part (the portion before `@`). Must be 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]` and must not start or end with a separator (`.`, `_`, `-`). Lowercased before use. If omitted, a random 10-character local part is generated.

domain.description: One of the server's configured domains (see `GET /api/domains`), or a **verified custom domain** — the latter requires that domain's `amd_…` claim token as the bearer token. Defaults to the first configured domain when omitted.

CreateAddressResponse.description: A newly created mailbox plus its one-time owner token.

owner_token.description: Bearer token proving ownership of this mailbox (`am_` + 43 base64url chars). Returned **only** here and from rotate — store it; it cannot be recovered. Required for extend, rotate, and all deletes.

RotateTokenResponse.description: The replacement owner token issued by a rotate; the previous token is already revoked.

owner_token.description: The new owner token. Same format and handling rules as at creation.

address.description: Full email address of the mailbox (lowercased).

expires_at.description: When the mailbox expires and becomes eligible for purging (UTC).

deleted.description: Number of messages that were deleted.

MessageSummary.description: Lightweight message representation used in inbox listings (no bodies or attachment metadata).

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if the email had no Subject header.

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

has_attachments.description: True if the message has one or more attachments.

seen.description: True once the message was marked read via the read endpoint.

AttachmentMeta.description: Attachment metadata returned alongside a full message. Download the bytes via the attachment endpoint.

id.description: Attachment identifier; use it in the download URL.

filename.description: Original filename, or null if the part had none.

content_type.description: MIME type of the attachment as parsed from the message.

size.description: Size of the attachment content in bytes.

StoredMessage.description: A fully materialised message including bodies and attachment metadata.

mailbox_address.description: Address of the mailbox this message belongs to.

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if absent.

message_date.description: Date parsed from the message's Date header (UTC), or null if missing/unparseable.

text_body.description: Plain-text body, or null if the message had none.
examples: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

html_body.description: HTML body, or null if the message had none. UNTRUSTED, attacker-controlled markup: anyone can email this mailbox, and the server stores and returns the HTML verbatim. Never inject it into a live DOM — render it inside a sandboxed iframe (`<iframe sandbox>` without `allow-scripts`) or sanitize it first (e.g. DOMPurify), and block remote content by default.
examples: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

raw_size.description: Size in bytes of the raw message as received over SMTP (DATA phase).

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

seen.description: True once the message was marked read via the read endpoint.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata (bytes downloaded separately). Empty when there are none.

MailEvent.description: Payload delivered in the `data` field of each SSE `message` event. Mirrors a MessageSummary plus the target `address` and the server-extracted verification code, giving enough to render an inbox row immediately; treat the REST listing as authoritative.

address.description: The mailbox address the message arrived for.

id.description: Identifier of the newly stored message.

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if absent.

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

has_attachments.description: True if the message has one or more attachments.

code.description: OTP / verification code the server extracted from the subject or text body, or null if none was detected. Normalized to bare digits for numeric codes (e.g. `G-482913` becomes `482913`).

VapidPublicKeyResponse.description: The server's VAPID public key for `PushManager.subscribe`.

PushConfigResponse.description: Which push channels this server can deliver on.

webpush.description: True when a VAPID keypair is configured (browsers/PWAs).

apns.description: True when APNs credentials are configured (native iOS apps).

SubscriptionKind.description: Push channel: `webpush` (W3C Web Push with VAPID) or `apns` (Apple Push Notification service).

SubscribeRequest.description: A push subscription of either kind. Web Push: `{ endpoint, keys }`, exactly as produced by `PushSubscription.toJSON()`. APNs: `{ device_token }`. `kind` is optional and inferred from which identifier is present.

endpoint.description: Web Push only: HTTPS push-service URL unique to this device/browser.

device_token.description: APNs only: the hex device token from `didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken`.

SubscribeResponse.description: Confirmation of a registered push subscription.

id.description: Server-side id of the subscription (stable across re-subscribes of the same endpoint/token).

UnsubscribeRequest.description: Identifies the subscription to remove: provide the Web Push `endpoint` or the APNs `device_token`.

endpoint.description: The push-service URL used at registration (Web Push).

device_token.description: The device token used at registration (APNs).

DomainsResponse.description: The set of domains the server accepts mail for.

domains.description: Configured domains; the first is the default for address creation.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the server is healthy.
Always `"ready"` when the storage backend answers queries.

Error.description: Uniform error envelope returned on any non-2xx response.

code.description: Optional machine-readable rejection code, present on policy errors: `pro_required`, `lifetime_cap`, `client_token_expired`, `client_token_invalid`. More codes may be added; ignore unknown ones.

TierPolicy.description: What one tier may do when entitlements are enforced. Clients should drive their gates and paywall copy from these numbers instead of hardcoding them.

active_mailboxes.description: Active-mailbox cap per attested device (`0` = unlimited). Reported now; enforced once attestation ships.

max_lifetime_seconds.description: Ceiling on a mailbox's total lifetime (`expires_at - created_at`) including extends, in seconds. `0` = unlimited.

custom_local_parts.description: May pick the local part instead of getting a random one.

domain_count.description: How many of the configured domains are usable, counted from the front of the `GET /api/domains` list. `0` = all.

VerifyEntitlementsRequest.description: Optional purchase proof. Omit the body (or the id) to mint a free-tier token.

rc_app_user_id.description: The app's anonymous RevenueCat app-user id. The server checks the pro entitlement against RevenueCat and caches the verdict briefly.

ClientTokenResponse.description: A freshly minted client token — from `POST /api/entitlements/verify` (unattested) or the attest/assert endpoints (attested). Send it as `X-Client-Token` on writes; refresh via the endpoint that minted it when it nears `expires_at`.

client_token.description: Signed tier token (JWT, HS256). Attested tokens additionally carry the device key id.

tier.description: The tier embedded in the token.

challenge.description: Opaque base64url string. Hash it (SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes) into the `clientDataHash` for `DCAppAttestService`, and echo it verbatim in the attest/assert request.
The challenge (verbatim) whose SHA-256 was used as `clientDataHash`.

rc_app_user_id.description: Optional anonymous RevenueCat app-user id for the tier check; omit for a free-tier token.

AssertRequest.description: Assertion-based refresh for an already-attested device.

challenge.description: The challenge (verbatim) whose SHA-256 was used as `clientDataHash`.

rc_app_user_id.description: Optional anonymous RevenueCat app-user id for the tier check; omit for a free-tier token.
